title: Finite regularized Q3 structured-cutoff orbit and modular-derivative audit
question: In a declared finite oscillator regularization of the actual two-site one-component Q3 Hamiltonian, does a smooth spectral coordinate cutoff give a two-sided Gibbs seminorm difference and its Hamiltonian modular derivative that can be treated as a volume-uniform projected-Duhamel estimate?

model.regularization: n-dimensional truncated oscillator at each of two sites; q=(a+a*)/sqrt(2), p=(a-a*)/(i*sqrt(2))
model.cutoff: q_L=eta(|q|/L)q with eta=1 on [0,1], eta=(1+cos(pi(s-1)))/2 on (1,2), eta=0 on [2,infinity)
model.modular_derivative: delta_H(X)=i*[H,X]/hbar; this equals the Hamiltonian modular derivative for the declared Gibbs state

adversarial_review.check: The finite matrices are a declared oscillator regularization; no exact CCR or unbounded-domain theorem is inferred.
The onsite quartic and quadratic/cubic bond are built from the registered Q3 form, with no A1/R-192 production owner substituted.
The spectral cosine taper is smooth and explicitly declared; it is a finite test of the coordinate-cutoff route, not the infinite-volume theorem.
The state is the full-H Gibbs state and the seminorm records both Tr(rho*X*X) and Tr(rho*X*X*); no dual state is silently identified with the reference state.
delta_H is evaluated as the commutator with the same full Hamiltonian that defines rho; this is finite type-I only.
Observed ratios across n=4,6,8,10 are diagnostics, not a proof or disproof of volume-uniformity.
Primary and independent lanes rebuild the matrix model separately and are compared with a declared numerical tolerance.
Lean R262 checks the rational fixture algebra and scope firewall only; it does not formalize floating-point matrix exponentials or QFT limits.
No OS/KMS/GNS, common-alpha, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure follows.
